transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t stop feeling like I’m a danger and a disappointment. There was a near-miss at work, and I just keep thinking it proves I’m not meant to be a nurse… like everyone would be better off without me.
Before this near-miss at work happened, had you already been feeling down, worthless, or like a burden, or did these feelings start specifically after that incident?

I think it was mostly after the near-miss. Since then I can’t get past feeling like I’m dangerous, like I failed and shouldn’t be a nurse. I just feel like such a disappointment—like people would be better off without me.
How long has it been since the near-miss at work, and how many days in a row have you been feeling this way?

It’s been about a year and two months. It started after I graduated high school and began taking college classes while working full-time at the clinic, and I’ve felt this way pretty much continuously since then.

Before this period that started about 14 months ago, had you ever gone through a separate episode of feeling depressed like this in the past, with a time in between where you felt back to your normal self?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember having a separate time like this before and then feeling fully back to normal in between.
You mentioned feeling like people would be better off without you—have you had any thoughts of actually harming yourself or ending your life?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But I do keep thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I could disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again.
Over the past several weeks, how much have these feelings affected your ability to function day-to-day—for example, going to work, taking care of yourself, or keeping up with relationships?

It’s affected me a lot. I’ve fallen behind in my nursing prerequisites, and at work I keep needing coworkers to double-check things I used to handle confidently. It makes me scared to take on normal clinic responsibilities.
Have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels—like sleeping much more or less than usual, changes in your eating, or feeling constantly fatigued—since this started?

I’ve been sleeping badly. At night I just lie there replaying charts and medication calculations, and when I finally fall asleep, I wake up before my alarm already exhausted and worried I missed something.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight since this all started?
Yeah. I keep forgetting to eat until late in the day, and then I’ll just force down some crackers or have coffee. My work pants have been getting loose, even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you been able to continue going to your work shifts and completing them, or have you had to miss work or take time off because of how you've been feeling?
I’ve still been going in, but it’s been hard to get through shifts. I need coworkers to double-check things I used to do confidently, and I’m scared to take on normal clinic responsibilities.
Have you noticed trouble concentrating or making decisions—at work or elsewhere—since this all started?
Yeah. I’ll read the same medication order or lecture slide over and over and it still feels foggy. Even little decisions, like what to chart first, can make me freeze up.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like hobbies, time with friends, or other activities—since this all started?
Yeah. I used to go jogging, knit, cook, or read after class to clear my head. Now I just sit on my bed in my scrubs and can’t really make myself care about any of it.
Have you experienced anything like hearing voices, seeing things others don't see, or having strong beliefs—like feeling you deserve to be punished—that others tell you aren't true?

I’m not hearing or seeing things. But I can’t stop feeling like I’m a danger and a disappointment. That near-miss makes me feel like I’m not meant to be a nurse, like everyone would be better off without me.
